construction: A kernel is submitted by runtime call1 with actual driver child2 before the completion operation.
Runtime call3 is a zero-byte logical memset on the same FIFO; it remains a logical submit and has no fabricated device effect.
Runtime call4 and driver child5 submit a nonzero 64-byte memset with a distinct effect.
The operation starts at runtime copy call6 entry; its driver child7 and 8-byte D2H effect are inside the operation.
Successful runtime stream sync call8 and driver child9 capture the preceding FIFO; Host-readable token17 follows the return.
A separate kernel submitted by calls60/61 only after Host completion is outside the captured set, even if it has the same stream.
limitations: CPU construction exercises the real v0.3 file consumer, not CUDA execution or SDK timestamp accuracy.
No independent guarantee of pure Host blocking, net device-caused stall, or removable latency is asserted.
Current single-FIFO consumer rejects unresolved incoming or cross-stream work; this reference does not grant a new cross-stream support rule.
A future target validation must bind its own original record identities to these predeclared logical members; synthetic IDs or times cannot be copied into target evidence.
